questions.q: Why is Subledger Accounting described as a "shared engine" rather than a Payables or AR feature?
options: Because Subledger Accounting does not generate any journal entries
Because it is actually a reporting tool, not an accounting engine
Because Payables, Receivables, Fixed Assets, and other subledgers all route through the same core XLA_ tables and logic
Because each subledger has its own separate copy of Subledger Accounting
questions.explain: Subledger Accounting (sometimes called the Financials Accounting Hub) is a single shared engine used by every subledger, not a per-module feature.

options: The business transaction (invoice, receipt, depreciation run, etc.) in a generic way SLA can work with regardless of its source subledger
A customer's bill-to site
The supplier's bank account
The ledger's chart of accounts
questions.explain: XLA_TRANSACTION_ENTITIES is the generic representation of the source transaction, independent of which subledger it came from.

questions.q: What decides how a specific accounting event gets turned into debits and credits?
options: A random assignment made at posting time
The business unit's security role
Hardcoded logic unique to each subledger module
Configured accounting rules on the ledger — mapping logic for which event produces which debit and credit
questions.explain: SLA applies each ledger's configured accounting rules to turn an event into the actual journal entry, which is why the same transaction type can post differently across different ledgers.

questions.q: What does XLA_DISTRIBUTION_LINKS allow you to trace?
options: A business unit back to its data access set
A subledger journal line back to the precise source distribution row that caused it
A supplier back to its bank account
A ledger back to its primary ledger
questions.explain: XLA_DISTRIBUTION_LINKS is the precise link between a subledger accounting journal line and its originating distribution.

questions.q: What benefit does the shared Subledger Accounting design provide across different subledgers?
options: It removes the need for accounting rules
No real benefit — each subledger still behaves completely differently
Consistent auditability: any journal line can be traced back through events to its original transaction, regardless of which subledger it started in
It eliminates the need for a General Ledger entirely
questions.explain: Because every subledger routes through the same engine and tables, the same tracing technique (distribution links -> events -> transaction entity) works no matter where a transaction originated.
